questions.prompt: In Application-Level Middleware, which statement best describes Global middleware with app.use()?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Middleware runs in registered order. Each function must end the response, call next() to continue, or forward an error; avoid accidentally doing more than one of these.
Treat the HTTP method and path as an API contract. Use the current Express 5 path syntax, validate captured values, and test both matching and non-matching requests.
questions.answer_key: Middleware runs in registered order. Each function must end the response, call next() to continue, or forward an error; avoid accidentally doing more than one of these.
questions.explanation: Middleware runs in registered order. Each function must end the response, call next() to continue, or forward an error; avoid accidentally doing more than one of these.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Application-Level Middleware?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Middleware executes in registration order. Each function should either complete the response, pass control, or forward an error; keep middleware responsibilities small and place parsing, security, routes, fallback, and error handlers intentionally.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: Middleware executes in registration order. Each function should either complete the response, pass control, or forward an error; keep middleware responsibilities small and place parsing, security, routes, fallback, and error handlers intentionally.
questions.explanation: Middleware executes in registration order. Each function should either complete the response, pass control, or forward an error; keep middleware responsibilities small and place parsing, security, routes, fallback, and error handlers intentionally.

questions.prompt: A change related to Application-Level Middleware appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
